title: Vision, Audition & Gestalt Perceptual Organization
description: Explore visual and auditory anatomy, photoreceptors, color vision theories, and Gestalt grouping laws.

slides.title: The Visual Apparatus 👁️
slides.content:
# The Retina & Photoreceptor Cells

Light passes through the **cornea**, enters the adjustable **pupil** (controlled by the colored **iris**), is focused by the **lens** via accommodation, and projects onto the **retina**.

| Characteristic | Rods | Cones |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Total Count** | ~120 million per eye | ~6 million per eye |
| **Retinal Location** | Periphery of retina | Clustered tightly in **fovea** (center) |
| **Sensitivity** | High in dim twilight (night vision) | Low in dim light; requires bright light |
| **Color & Detail** | Monochromatic (black & white); coarse | Color vision; high fine-detail visual acuity |

quizData.question: Which photoreceptor cells are concentrated in the fovea, function best in bright illumination, and provide color vision and high spatial acuity?
quizData.explanation: Cones operate in daylight conditions, perceive color, and provide sharp central focus inside the fovea.

slides.title: Theories of Color Vision 🎨
slides.content:
## How We See the Spectrum

1. **Trichromatic Theory** (Young-Helmholtz): The retina contains three distinct types of cones, each maximally sensitive to one of three primary wavelengths: **Red (long)**, **Green (medium)**, and **Blue (short)**. Mixing these signals produces all perceived colors.
2. **Opponent-Process Theory** (Ewald Hering): Visual neurons in the thalamus and cortex process colors in antagonistic pairs:
   * **Red vs. Green**
   * **Blue vs. Yellow**
   * **Black vs. White**

Staring at a green square fatigues green receptors, producing a vivid **red afterimage** when looking at a blank white wall!

slides.title: Gestalt Laws of Perceptual Organization 🖼️
slides.content:
## How the Mind Structures Visual Scenes

* **Figure-Ground**: Distinguishing the primary object (figure) from the surrounding background (ground).
* **Proximity**: Grouping nearby figures together.
* **Similarity**: Grouping elements that share visual attributes (color, shape).
* **Continuity**: Perceiving smooth, continuous lines rather than discontinuous, jagged segments.
* **Closure**: Filling in subjective gaps to create a complete, whole object.

### Depth Perception
* **Binocular Cues**: Retinal Disparity (distance between the two eyes creates two slightly different retinal angles; brain computes depth).
* **Monocular Cues**: Linear perspective, relative size, interposition (overlap), and motion parallax.

quizData.question: When viewing an incomplete circle with a tiny missing gap, your visual system automatically perceives a complete circle. Which Gestalt principle is demonstrated?
quizData.explanation: The principle of closure describes our brain's tendency to fill in gaps to create complete, whole forms.

slides.title: Auditory Architecture Hook 👂
slides.content:
## Sound Transduction in the Cochlea

Sound waves vibrate the eardrum, oscillate the three middle ear ossicles (**Hammer, Anvil, Stirrup** / Malleus, Incus, Stapes), and push fluid against the **basilar membrane** within the spiral **cochlea**. Microscopic hair cells on the basilar membrane bend, firing action potentials up the auditory nerve to the temporal lobe!
